g.text: How a stored key is composed, and who can read it back afterwards.
inside a mount, so the scope is the definition
the defaults are the safe answers
The key is <definitionId>:<name>, never scoped by mount token, so two mounts of one definition read one record.
The g field fences a user-retained record to one session generation: a record written under another generation reads as absent.
storage decides how long the browser keeps it; retention decides who may read it back
Outside a mount, useStoredState resolves to
the reserved @host scope. No definition can
claim that name: @ is not a legal character
The one thing to get right
retention: 'browser' opts out of the wipe
Nothing clears it, which also means every
user of this browser profile reads the same
value. It is for a display density or a
collapsed panel, never for anything derived
the choice that can leak state between users
